mechanism_narrative: The ongoing rise in WORKPLACES mobility lifts nearby daytime spending and lunch traffic, so RETAIL_REC should improve over the next four weeks if the work-return trend continues.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES keeps rising or stays elevated but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the last four weeks, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained substitution toward RESIDENTIAL time signals more home-based activity and less discretionary shopping, which should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline and RETAIL_REC rises instead of falling over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT moves above the local commuting threshold, it expands access to shopping districts and raises retail visitation within one week, increasing RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above 0 and remains above 0 for at least two weekly observations
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is above zero for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays strongly positive while PARKS stays depressed, households are likely concentrating trips on essentials rather than discretionary outings, which should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent level over four weeks.
failure_condition: If high GROCERY_PHARM coincides with persistently low PARKS and RETAIL_REC nonetheless rises over the next 28 days, this mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, a decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reduces day-trip volume and should lower retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent late-year uplift in GROCERY_PHARM combined with flat RETAIL_REC indicates holiday-prep spending is being redirected away from discretionary retail, so retail-and-recreation mobility should soften over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated into the next month but RETAIL_REC increases rather than weakens, the seasonal substitution claim is false.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS rebounds from its depressed level, it signals broader amenity use and weekend out-of-home activity, which should spill over into higher retail-and-recreation mobility within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from one weekly mean to the next
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by 5 points or more and RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES keeps recovering while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, the combination implies partial re-occupation but not full normalization, which should produce only a modest upward drift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to improve while RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean within 28 days, the hypothesis fails.
